solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Family member's containers taken across lake by crew

indicators.note: the containers are carried over and around the lake, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: cans are containers
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A family member's tins are ferried over a lake by a boat's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken across' puts L inside CANS, giving CLANS, before MAN. The 's of the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Scottish clan, a kinship group, is one belonging to that extended family.

clue.text: Libertine reluctant to go on a Spanish river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of what follows, so it goes on it

parts.note: loth is an old spelling of loath, meaning reluctant
rio is the Spanish word for river

explanation.surface: A rake who is unwilling to sail on a river in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, LOTH placed 'on' A RIO means above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, the seducer in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, became a byword for a womanising libertine.

clue.text: Like some of Stravinsky's music — so nice, Callas recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered up again in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The soprano Maria Callas remembers some Stravinsky pieces as lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered, but read as re-collected it signals the letters of SO NICE CALLAS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's middle period, such as Pulcinella, revived eighteenth-century forms and is described as the revivalist style of that name.

clue.text: Russian port's odd, turning fellow sailors back ultimately

indicators.note: turning the word round means it is read backwards

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
a man is a fellow

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A Russian harbour seems strange because its sailors keep coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses RUM to MUR; 'ultimately' takes S and K, the last letters of 'sailors' and 'back'. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmansk is the ice-free harbour city on the Kola Peninsula in Russia's far north-west.

clue.text: Representation of an elf initially said to evoke water nymphs

indicators.note: a representation is a new rendering, so the letters that follow are rearranged
initially points to the first letter of the word elf

explanation.surface: Describing an elf, as spoken, is supposed to call up water spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representation of' rearranges AN, E (from 'initially' on 'elf') and SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the naiads were nymphs presiding over springs, rivers and lakes; this is the classical plural form.

clue.text: A niece regularly eating fish — and mushroom for example

indicators.note: one piece eats the other, taking it inside
regularly picks every other letter of the word niece

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A niece keeps eating fish, plus a mushroom, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes I and C from 'niece'; A IC then is 'eating' GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers gilled fungi of the type whose common field variety is the familiar edible mushroom.

clue.text: Control farm animal upset about start of rainstorm

indicators.note: about means surrounding the letter that follows
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal

indicators.note: start of points to the first letter of rainstorm

explanation.surface: Keep hold of a farm animal spooked by a downpour starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PIG into GIP, which goes 'about' R, the 'start of' rainstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a grip on something is to have control or a firm hold of it.

clue.text: A second gathering assembled unethically

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a second
a rally is a gathering of assembled people

explanation.surface: Briefly, a crowd assembled in an immoral way.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is informal British for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act without regard to morals is to act unethically, outside right and wrong.

clue.text: Swedish physicist's torment, having reduced capital

parts.note: angst is anguish or torment

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A Swedish scientist suffers because his capital has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims ROME to ROM. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Jonas Ångström was the Swedish pioneer of spectroscopy; a tiny unit of length is named after him.

clue.text: German fellow, abstemious type, wearing pair of spectacles

indicators.note: the abstemious type has the spectacles on, so is enclosed by them

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters O O
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober German man in glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: TT 'wearing' a pair of O-shaped lenses sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's given name, as in Bismarck.

clue.text: Arrive with a harvester — and have a terrible fall!

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a cropper is one who gathers crops

explanation.surface: Turning up with a reaper and then taking a nasty tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom originally meant a heavy fall from a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tumble badly, or more loosely to suffer a sudden failure.

clue.text: Inclination of a revolutionary head to support homework

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting pieces sit below the one they hold up

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework
a red is a communist revolutionary
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A rebel leader's inclination to back up schoolwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to support' means the later pieces sit beneath homework. 'head' is a headland, not a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiness, a disposition to act, is a sense of inclination as well as of being prepared.

clue.text: Old way to introduce a popular decree

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An old method of bringing in a well-liked ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order officially, to issue a ruling with authority.

clue.text: Avoidance of champ inspired by eastern girl

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the champ is taken inside

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name
to champ is to chew

explanation.surface: A champion steers clear, motivated by a girl from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a champion but is the verb to munch; CHEW is 'inspired by' E SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to shun or keep away from, and this noun is the act of shunning.

clue.text: Abandon doctor, sheltering horse he lost

indicators.note: sheltering means keeping inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to doctor is to falsify or fake

indicators.note: lost means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Desert a vet who looked after a horse he has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he lost' takes H and E from HORSE, leaving ORS, which FAKE is 'sheltering'.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake someone is to desert or give them up.

clue.text: Perennial plant not many associated with disease

indicators.note: associated with joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: a fever is an illness
few means not many

explanation.surface: A long-lived plant thought to be linked with a handful of illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives FEW first, but the disease leads in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This daisy-like herb of the chrysanthemum family is a long-lived garden and medicinal species.

clue.text: Princes, for example, demanding author's share of profits

definitions.meaning: princes are among the members of a reigning family
a writer is paid a percentage of each sale of the book

explanation.surface: Princes insisting on their cut of a writer's earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both royal persons collectively and a payment to an author per copy sold.

clue.text: Part of target, securing free escort

indicators.note: securing means holding something inside, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: the outer is the ring of an archery target outside the inner rings
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: An archer frees part of the target to guard someone.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTER is 'securing' RID.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist riding beside a dignitary's car is a guard travelling alongside as an escort.

clue.text: German dance craze abandoned by head of major African state?

parts.note: Tanz is the German word for dance

indicators.note: abandoned by means the craze loses the letter named

parts.note: a mania is a craze

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of major

explanation.surface: A German dance fad dropped by a major's leader in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' removes M ('head of' major) from MANIA, leaving ANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanzania is a country of East Africa, formed from Tanganyika and Zanzibar.

clue.text: Funny way Guyanese extremists managed to get caught

indicators.note: the managed piece gets caught between the others, held inside them

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: extremists points to the outermost letters of Guyanese

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: Odd how fringe Guyanese radicals contrived to be arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' means odd, not amusing; 'extremists' takes the outer letters of Guyanese, and 'to get caught' holds managed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny here means peculiar or odd, not amusing.

clue.text: Female spy taking in new peer

parts.note: Vi is a woman's name

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing the next letter

parts.note: a scout is one sent to spy

explanation.surface: A woman spy recruits a new aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' is a noble, not a verb meaning to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British noble ranking between earl and baron.

clue.text: Posh sun-hat adapted principally for an idyllic place

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage, as opposed to non-U
a topi is a pith helmet worn against the sun

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of adapted

explanation.surface: A smart sun hat altered chiefly for a perfect resort.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were the 1950s British labels for upper-class and middle-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary island gave its name to any perfect society or place.

clue.text: Old maid of diminutive size swigging whiskey

indicators.note: swigging means drinking down, taking the letter inside

parts.note: teeny means tiny
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tiny spinster downing her whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old maid' suggests a spinster, but here is a servant of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A between-maid was a junior servant assisting both cook and housemaid, a role of past Victorian households.

clue.text: Proper setting for further allotment

parts.note: real means genuine or proper
a location is a setting, as for a film

explanation.surface: The right place for another plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh distribution of resources or space is a new allotment of them.

clue.text: The first person a state prosecutor married

parts.note: a DA, district attorney, is a US state prosecutor

explanation.surface: The first person a prosecutor wed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, he was the first human God created.

clue.text: High-flyer in Navy plugging point repeatedly

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the navy goes between the points
repeatedly means the point is given twice

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A high achiever in the navy keeps making his point.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is 'plugging' the two Es from 'point repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed sea eagle soars high, and is a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Demanding old flame once treading the boards

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to tread the boards is to perform on stage

explanation.surface: A needy former lover who used to be on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means requiring great effort or precision, hard to satisfy.

clue.text: Old Italian's endless faith in English jail

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: trust is faith

explanation.surface: An ancient Italian's dwindling belief while locked in an English prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims TRUST to TRUS, which goes 'in' E CAN. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans inhabited Etruria in central Italy before Roman dominance.
